items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And it was when I first started doing Arbors jazz parties and they first invited me to play with whoever... And so we had one set and Michael Moore was leading the set... we all stood up and rehearsed in the morning. And we all took a part and played on the stage two or three pieces.

ctx.x: Well that was the next guy I was going to ask you about. Were you able to rub elbows with Milt Hinton?

That’s all I was able to do. Because when I started going to Arbors jazz parties and I started to see him play he was already in a wheelchair. I remember one quick story, have you got time for that? There was an Arbors jazz party almost a decade ago, maybe nine years ago, maybe ten years ago now. And it was when I first started doing Arbors jazz parties and they first invited me to play with whoever. You know, not to play with Diva or FivePlay and the other bands, but to actually play with whomever. Which was a…

parties. Because we were all on the same page. And it was a standing ovation. It was like one of those, you know what I mean, it’s like, if a promoter came and said we’re going to do this, it might not have come out so eloquent and so natural. You know it was bass players doing their tribute, the way they wanted to do it. So that’s my memory of Milt and seeing him towards the end. And at the end of that set he got up and sang “Old Man Time.”
